introduction: ERC-7053 defines an interoperable indexing method for recording, discovering, and retrieving the history of digital media across EVM-compatible blockchains. It was proposed by Bofu Chen and Tammy Yang in May 2023. The standard pairs a decentralized Content Identifier (CID) for each media file with a commit function that emits a Commit event and logs the block number of every commit, letting any system associate all on-chain data about the same content and trace it from creation to its current state.
designPurpose: ERC-7053 was designed to remove the fragmentation caused by the lack of a universal, interoperable identifier for digital media content. Before it, a file's metadata, storage location, and provenance lived in separate systems with no shared key, making cross-contract and cross-chain retrieval difficult. By anchoring each file to a cryptographic Content Identifier and standardizing one commit function with an indexed Commit event, it gives every system a predictable way to index and search the same content.
commonUsage: ERC-7053 is intended for digital media platforms, provenance registries, and content indexers that track the history of images, video, and other files on-chain. Because the Commit event indexes both the recorder and the asset CID, off-chain services can subscribe to it and rebuild a full timeline for each asset. The specification also describes indexing media referenced by NFTs by converting the file behind a tokenURI into the same CID, so ERC-721 and ERC-1155 collections can share one scheme.
fn.commit.desc: Registers a commit for the asset identified by assetCid. Emits a Commit event and records the block number of the commit for the provided assetCid, then returns that block number.
fn.commit.params.assetCid: The content identifier (CID) of the asset being committed.
fn.commit.params.commitData: The data associated with the commit.
fn.commit.returns.blockNumber: The block number at which the commit was made.
fn.Commit.desc: Emitted when a new commit is made, so indexers can track the recorder, the asset, and the commit data. The recorder and assetCid are indexed for filtering.
fn.Commit.params.recorder: The address of the account making the commit.
fn.Commit.params.assetCid: The content identifier of the asset being committed.
fn.Commit.params.commitData: The data associated with the commit.
sim.commitWalkthrough.name: Commit Media Walkthrough
sim.commitWalkthrough.desc: Follow a commit call from the recorder through the log mapping to the Commit event.
sim.commitWalkthrough.step.call: The recorder calls commit(assetCid, commitData) on the registry contract to index a media file.
sim.commitWalkthrough.step.execute: The contract appends the current block number to the recordLogs entry for the asset CID, building its on-chain history.
sim.commitWalkthrough.step.event: The contract emits Commit(recorder, assetCid, commitData) so off-chain indexers can update their timeline for the asset.
